svg.text: Azure AI Native Governance — Architecture v2.0
One flow: an agent asks → the gateway decides → the decision is logged as evidence.
SIMULATED tenant: Nordlicht GmbH • Synthetic data only • No live Azure tenant access
Gateway = FastAPI app (local lab) + OPA server :8181 + human-approval queue. Native decision at every step: none.
1 subscription • 4 resource groups (rg-test in eastus — outside allowed regions)
6 VMs • 8 storage accounts (2 public blob) • 3 Key Vaults (4 expired secrets)
4 AI resources (Azure OpenAI + AI Foundry hub + Content Safety + 1 unfiltered test)
20 Entra users (3 without MFA) • 6 Azure Policy assignments
Defender for Cloud: secure score 62% • AI data residency: EU only
28 controls — ISO/IEC 42001 + EU AI Act • 12 risks
WHAT AZURE NATIVE DOES — 10 services, one CAN line each
Every one of them admits the same thing, in red: it CANNOT decide one tool call.
CAN: Deny a resource in a
CAN: Score the estate, flag risks
CAN: RBAC on secrets, expire secrets
CAN: Register + run an agent with tools
CAN: Block a port, force a
CAN: Block Copilot on labelled content
16 CHECKS AZ-01 – AZ-16 — 0 Pass, 8 Fail, 8 Partial
AZ-16 is Partial BY DESIGN — it can only pass when a gateway like this one is in front of the tools.
DEMO — what the gateway decides (lab run)
Native decision in every case: none
NONE of them decides an individual
MCP tool call. That is the gap
Source of truth: app/data.py + app/checks.py. Every box above is in that code — nothing invented.
Deliberately NOT shown: Application Gateway, Azure Firewall, Web App, Function App, Queue, Redis, Cosmos DB,
SQL Database, Blob, Azure AI Search, VNet topology, Microsoft Foundry project box, Foundry Agent Service
dependencies, DDoS Protection, Application Insights — none of those are in the project code.
Legend: → request / data flow Green 1–5 = numbered steps Amber box = gateway decision Red = Fail / blocked
Azure native applications govern resources, identity, network and model content — none of them decides an individual MCP tool call.
